finding.question: Did Nancy Pelosi say the quoted words about US employers cutting hours, and what was the context of any matching or closely related statement?
finding.summary: The search found no contemporaneous recording or transcript supporting the attributed quotation. An unsourced 2013 blog repeated those words, but a recording and contemporaneous report show Pelosi using different words in 2010. She described the Affordable Care Act as enabling people to leave a job and pursue creative work while retaining health coverage; she did not say in that statement that employer-imposed cuts to hours were good.

sources.title: Pelosi to Aspiring Musicians: Quit Your Job, Taxpayers Will Cover Your Health Care
sources.snippet:
“We see it as an entrepreneurial bill,” Pelosi said, “a bill that says to someone, if you want to be creative and be a musician or whatever, you can leave your work, focus on your talent, your skill, your passion, your aspirations because you will have health care.” 

 Pelosi made the remarks while speaking at the Capitol on Wednesday to the Asian American and Pacific Islanders Summit.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's Message to America's Youth
sources.snippet:
(BEGIN VIDEO CLIP)

SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE NANCY PELOSI, D-CALIF.: We see it as an entrepreneurial bill — a bill that says to someone, if you want to be creative and be a musician or whatever, you can leave your work, focus on your talent, your skill, your passion, your aspirations because you will have health care.

(END VIDEO CLIP)

finding.question: Was Nancy Pelosi Speaker of the US House when she made the statement quoted or most closely matching the claim?
finding.summary: In a closely matching CNN interview published on September 22, 2013, Pelosi discussed concerns about the 40-hour workweek and described the freedom to follow one’s passion. Contemporary reporting and official House press releases identify her then as House Democratic leader, not Speaker. The exact wording in the claim appears in a 2018 article, but that article does not date or source the purported quotation.

sources.title: Pelosi to Crowley: Hillary more prepared to be President than Obama was
sources.snippet: CROWLEY: Let me ask you then about Obamacare, itself. Coming up for a big date on Obamacare October 1st when people can begin to sign up through the — marketplaces. Do you have any reservations at all? Are you worried at all? And I ask you this because you know union leaders, I mean, James Hoffa is one of those who wrote a letter to you and said Obamacare is now stands would, quote, “destroy the foundation of the 40-hour work week.” ... This is life, healthy life, liberty, the freedom to pursue your happiness which could be follow your passion for good rather than follow your palate and be constrained by your policy.

report_raw.claim: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said of US employers, “Employers cutting hours is a good thing. It then gives that person time to pursue their dreams and passions.”
report_raw.justification: The exact quotation appears in a 2013 blog post and a 2018 article, but neither excerpt identifies a recording or transcript for it. [S3][S7] In a recorded 2010 statement, Pelosi used different words to argue that health coverage would let people leave work and pursue creative ambitions. [S2] A 2013 CNN interview also linked health coverage and the freedom to follow one’s passion, after a question about concerns over the 40-hour workweek, but the supplied excerpt does not contain the claimed quotation. [S4] Pelosi was identified as Speaker in the 2010 clip and as Democratic leader in 2013; the exact attributed quotation cannot be assigned a date from the available evidence. [S2][S5][S6] Inference: The attributed words are unsubstantiated, but the excerpts do not definitively establish that she never said them.
key_points: The two supplied publications that use the exact quotation do not identify an underlying recording or transcript. [S3][S7]
A 2010 video clip records different remarks about leaving work to pursue creative ambitions while retaining health care. [S2]
A 2013 CNN interview contains related language about pursuing a passion, but its supplied excerpt is not the claimed quotation. [S4]
The findings label the quotation refuted, but the available excerpts do not rule out an unidentified occasion on which it was said. [S2][S4]
report_raw.counter_argument: A refuted verdict is plausible because the identifiable 2010 and 2013 remarks use different language, while the exact quotation appears in unsourced secondary accounts. [S2][S3][S4][S7] It was not adopted because those excerpts do not conclusively disprove that Pelosi said the quoted words on another occasion.
evidence_gaps: A dated, complete recording or transcript of the alleged employer-hours statement, or an authoritative investigation tracing the quotation to a misquotation, would materially firm up the verdict.
The exact quotation could not be tied to an identifiable date, so Pelosi’s office at the time of that alleged statement cannot be independently established.
